newsitem.title: USA: Latest Kennedy scandal cuts voter support - poll.
newsitem.headline: Latest Kennedy scandal cuts voter support - poll.

text.p: Representative Joseph Kennedy's lead over Republican rivals in a potential Massachusetts governor's race has vanished amid family controversies including allegations his brother had an affair with a 14-year old babysitter, according to poll results released Wednesday.
Kennedy, a Democrat who is preparing a bid for the 1998 governor's race, has lost a huge lead he enjoyed four months ago over Lt. Gov. Paul Cellucci, the Boston Globe reported.

Before the latest Kennedy family controversies arose, it appeared that his only serious rival in the race would be Gov. William Weld, who said this weekend he would accept the post of ambassador to Mexico rather than run for a third term.

But Cellucci now leads the congressman by 42 percent to 37 percent, a statistical dead heat within the poll's margin of error of plus-or-minus five percentage points. In a matchup against State Treasurer Joseph Malone, Kennedy is ahead 40 percent to 38 percent, according to the poll.

The Boston Globe, quoting unnamed sources, reported Friday that Michael Kennedy had had an affair with his children's 14-year-old babysitter. Michael Kennedy's office did not return phone calls seeking comment.

Joseph Kennedy's campaign has also been bruised by his first wife, Sheila Rauch Kennedy, who is on a national tour to promote her book, "Shattered Faith," about her opposition to the October 1996 annulment of their marriage.
The Boston Globe and WBZ-TV survey of 400 likely Massachusetts voters was conducted on April 28-29.
